titulo: What Happens If You Stop Eating? The 382-Day Fast #shorts
premisa: Título: 'What Happens If You Stop Eating? The 382-Day Fast' (47 car.). Guion de ~140 palabras, 52-56 s. ESCALADA 1, tu cuerpo: 'You stop eating. One man did it for 382 days — and doctors let him.' → 'Hour 24: your sugar reserves are gone. Your body starts burning fat. On purpose.' → 'Day 3: your breath smells fruity. That's ketones. Your brain is running on fat now.' → 'Here's the weird part: the hunger fades.' ESCALADA 2, entras en la historia sin ficha: 'Now you're in Scotland, 1965. You weigh 456 pounds. You walk into a hospital in Dundee and say: I'm done eating.' → 'Doctors expect a few days. You keep going.' → 'Tea. Coffee. Sparkling water. Vitamins. Nothing else.' ESCALADA 3, lo absurdo: 'You still work at your dad's fish and chip shop. Frying food. All day.' → 'You go to the bathroom once every 40 to 50 days. Doctors wrote that down.' ESCALADA 4, riesgo controlado: 'Without potassium and salt pills, your heart could stop. So they check your blood. Again. And again.' ESCALADA 5, final: 'Month after month, you just shrink. 456 pounds… 300… 180.' → 'Then you eat again: one boiled egg and a slice of bread and butter.' CIERRE: 'Total: 382 days. 276 pounds gone. The longest fast in medical records.' Corte. Todos los datos están documentados en el informe de Stewart y Fleming (Postgraduate Medical Journal, 1973) y en Guinness.
gancho: You stop eating. One man did it for 382 days — and doctors let him.
